items.title: Direct summands of an m-pseudo-coherent complex are m-pseudo-coherent
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that if a direct sum of two complexes is m-pseudo-coherent then so is each summand. The proof uses the decomposition of the diagonal triangle for a direct sum into the sum of the two trivial triangles for the summands, so that the cone lemma produces m-pseudo-coherence of a shifted direct sum of one summand with itself; iterating gives m-pseudo-coherence of all successive shifts of that summand, and for large shifts the characterisation of m-pseudo-coherence makes the single shifted summand m-pseudo-coherent. Working backwards through the distinguished triangles relating consecutive shifts yields m-pseudo-coherence of the summand itself, and the pseudo-coherent case follows from the characterisation.
